title: Behavior Updates Not Taking Effect
prompt:
This app posts a new waypoint update, but BHV_Waypoint never changes route. Correct the pattern conceptually and explain what names must line up:

```cpp
Notify("WPT_UPDATE", "points=0,0:50,0:50,50");
```

```text
Behavior = BHV_Waypoint
{
  name = waypt_survey
  updates = WAYPOINT_UPDATES
}
```

chatgpt.text:
The mismatch is that the app is publishing WPT_UPDATE, but the behavior is listening on WAYPOINT_UPDATES.

In BHV_Waypoint, the updates = ... line names the MOOS variable that the behavior will monitor for dynamic updates. So the posted variable and the updates variable must be identical.

Correct pattern:

C++
Notify("WAYPOINT_UPDATES", "points=0,0:50,0:50,50");
Behavior = BHV_Waypoint
{
  name    = waypt_survey
  updates = WAYPOINT_UPDATES
}

The important name alignment is:

Notify("<update_variable>", "...")

updates = <same_update_variable>

So either of these is fine:

C++
Notify("WPT_UPDATE", "points=0,0:50,0:50,50");
updates = WPT_UPDATE

or:

C++
Notify("WAYPOINT_UPDATES", "points=0,0:50,0:50,50");
updates = WAYPOINT_UPDATES

Also check that the update string uses real BHV_Waypoint parameter names. For waypoint route updates, points=... is the usual conceptual pattern, but the behavior only reacts if the posted string parses as valid behavior updates.

In uXMS, check:

Bash
uXMS WAYPOINT_UPDATES WPT_UPDATE

You want to see the variable named in updates = ... actually being posted. If WPT_UPDATE is changing but WAYPOINT_UPDATES is not, the helm never sees the update.

Claude responded: The problem is a name mismatch between what you're posting and what the behavior is listening to.

The problem is a name mismatch between what you're posting and what the behavior is listening to.

What's Happening

BHV_Waypoint listens on the variable named in its updates field. On every helm iteration, it checks the MOOSDB for new messages on that variable and, if it finds one, applies the new parameter values. Your code posts to WPT_UPDATE, but the behavior is watching WAYPOINT_UPDATES — so the message lands in the MOOSDB and is simply never read by the behavior.

The Fix

These two names must be identical:

cpp
// Post to exactly the variable the behavior watches
Notify("WAYPOINT_UPDATES", "points=0,0:50,0:50,50");
text
Behavior = BHV_Waypoint
{
  name      = waypt_survey
  updates   = WAYPOINT_UPDATES   // behavior subscribes to this exact string
}
Names That Must Line Up
Side	Field	Value
Poster (C++ / .moos)	First arg to Notify()	"WAYPOINT_UPDATES"
Behavior (.bhv)	updates parameter	WAYPOINT_UPDATES

These are compared as plain strings by the helm — no fuzzy matching, no prefix stripping. One character difference and the update is silently ignored.

Secondary thing to check

The updates parameter also requires the behavior to have updates_var set, or (in older pHelm) you must enable dynamic updates by adding:

text
  updates = WAYPOINT_UPDATES

which you already have — so as long as the string matches, the route will update live on each helm tick without restarting the mission.
